title: Regulatory change radar
note: Curated, read-only diff between Wapsi's legal baseline (MHA/I4C SOP, 02.01.2026) and new or pending rules. Rows are written by hand from the primary documents, never generated by an LLM at run time. Every quote is verbatim (<= 25 words) and is re-verified against the raw documents by `uv run python -m wapsi.search.check_citations` (fetch with `uv run python -m wapsi.search.radar fetch`; restamp with `uv run python -m wapsi.search.radar verify --write`). Nothing here changes Wapsi's rules: each suggested action waits for a human decision (review.status).

evidence.quote: Shri Bandi Sanjay Kumar in a written reply to a question in the Lok Sabha.

clauses.title: Which holds the RBI DRAFT covers

new.quote: applies to Suspected Money Mule Transactions or Account, save where the temporary debit is placed or continued pursuant to a specific instruction of an LEA

baseline.quote: This SOP is valid only for cybercrime complaints reported on NCRP including 1930 and escalated to CFCFRMS.
All such requests escalated through CFCFRMS shall be accompanied by notices delivered electronically under the afore mentioned provisions.

clauses.applies_to: Holds a bank places on its own transaction-monitoring flags. Holds placed or continued on a specific LEA instruction stay outside the RBI DRAFT's procedure.
clauses.impact: Every Wapsi hold starts from an NCRP complaint escalated to CFCFRMS, which arrives with an LEA notice. Those holds sit in the RBI DRAFT's carve-out and stay on the SOP track (90-day clock). The RBI DRAFT's procedure would matter only if the bank also placed holds on its own monitoring flags.
clauses.suggested_action: Keep CFCFRMS holds on the SOP track. Record the CFCFRMS / LEA notice reference on each hold so the carve-out can be shown to an auditor.

rules: Every hold comes from an NCRP / CFCFRMS complaint and follows the SOP

clauses.title: Maximum length of a hold

new.quote: Maximum duration … in the absence of any contrary instruction from an LEA or Competent Authority is 60 days from the date of temporary debit hold

baseline.quote: the bank may remove the hold, after completion of 90 calendar days from the date of amount put on hold.
they may ask for an extension for continuation for up to 90 additional calendar days.

clauses.applies_to: Bank-initiated holds without a contrary LEA or competent-authority instruction.
clauses.impact: A bank-initiated hold would end by day 60 unless an LEA or competent authority says otherwise. CFCFRMS holds keep the SOP's 90 calendar days, extendable by up to 90 more on the LEA's request.
clauses.suggested_action: If the RBI DRAFT is adopted, track a 60-day maximum for bank-initiated holds only, as a separate clock. Leave the SOP hold-lapse clock unchanged for CFCFRMS holds.

rules: Hold-lapse clock: 90 calendar days, LEA intimated 15 days before lapse (SOP 10.1)

clauses.title: Holder's explanation and the bank's decision

new.quote: The bank shall give 20 days' time from the date of Temporary Debit Hold to the account holder for submission of the explanation / justification.
In case no explanation is received, the bank shall take decision, within 30 days from date of temporary debit hold.
The bank shall remove the debit hold on the 31st day from the date of reference to the LEA.

baseline.quote: submit such a grievance at the earliest and not beyond 07 calendar days from the day the aggrieved person complains.
remove the hold on the reported amount within 15 calendar days of the receipt of the grievance.

clauses.impact: The RBI DRAFT makes the bank itself ask the holder for an explanation and decide, then refer the case to the police through NCRP-CFCFRMS and release the hold if no instruction follows. Under the SOP the holder complains through the bank and the IO decides.
clauses.suggested_action: No change for CFCFRMS holds. If the bank adopts bank-initiated holds, add the explanation, decision and release milestones as their own clocks after a supervisor approves.

clauses.title: Unknowing mules and the STR

new.para: Annex III, 3(vi) (definition of Money Mule Account)
new.quote: an account used, knowingly or unknowingly, to receive, layer or transfer proceeds of cyber-enabled financial fraud on behalf of another person.
established that an account opened and operated is that of a Money Mule, but STR was not filed … deemed that the bank has not complied
The bank shall continue to file Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs) with FIU-IND under extant instructions; this SOP does not modify those obligations.

baseline.quote: An IO must take into account the possibility of reported accounts being operated without the knowledge or connivance or consent of the account holder

clauses.applies_to: Accounts Wapsi classifies as innocent holders (SOP 5(xii)): bona fide recipients and unwitting conduits.
clauses.impact: Under the RBI DRAFT an account used knowingly or unknowingly to receive, layer or transfer fraud proceeds on behalf of another person is a Money Mule Account, and not filing an STR once an account is established as a mule counts as non-compliance. Wapsi files no automatic STR on either kind of innocent holder: the officer decides, and Wapsi recommends an STR where the account was used as a conduit (an unwitting conduit), the case the RBI DRAFT's "unknowingly" limb covers. A bona fide recipient that kept the money as payment gets no STR recommendation by default.
clauses.suggested_action: Supervisor to confirm, before the RBI DRAFT takes effect, that bona fide recipients fall outside its mule definition (they kept the money as payment, not on behalf of another person), and that the officer's STR decision on every conduit is recorded in the EDD memo. Rules stay as they are while the text is a DRAFT.

rules: Innocent holder (SOP 5(xii)): hold the amount, no escalation, EDD memo; no automatic STR, the officer decides
Unwitting conduit: STR recommended for the officer's decision; bona fide recipient: no STR by default

clauses.title: Nodal, pool and escrow accounts

new.quote: not apply to nodal accounts, pool accounts, escrow accounts, or other special-purpose accounts, e.g., dividend, share capital.

baseline.quote: where CFCFRMS notifies for action against a nodal, escrow, or pool account, the bank shall hold the disputed amount
Such holds shall not be applied to nodal, pool and escrow accounts.

clauses.applies_to: Holds on nodal, pool and escrow accounts.
clauses.impact: The RBI DRAFT's bank-initiated holds cannot be used on nodal, pool or escrow accounts. Wapsi holds only the disputed amount in such accounts, on the CFCFRMS notice, so nothing changes.
clauses.suggested_action: No rule change. Keep every nodal / pool hold tied to its CFCFRMS notice; never re-place it as a bank-initiated hold.

rules: Nodal / pool / escrow: hold the disputed amount only; no forward hold (SOP 9.1(i), 9.1(iii))

clauses.title: Whole-account holds only as a last resort

new.quote: the temporary debit hold at the account level shall be applied as a last resort and only in exceptional circumstances
place a Temporary Debit Hold on the Suspected Money Mule Transaction or, if the account is a Suspected Money Mule Account, on the entire account.

baseline.quote: Unwarranted orders for freezing accounts shall be discouraged, and accountability measures shall be established.

clauses.impact: The RBI DRAFT still allows a hold on a whole suspected-mule account, but only as a last resort in exceptional circumstances. Wapsi's holds are amount-specific by default; account-level action exists only as a recorded, supervisor-approved exception (an officer's request with at least one reason from a closed list, approved by a different supervisor), and Wapsi never emits one automatically. That fits both texts.
clauses.suggested_action: No rule change; keep amount-specific holds by default and the maker-checker exception for account-level holds.

rules: Amount-specific holds by default: hold the tainted amount only, min(tainted, balance) (SOP 5(ix), 9.1)
Account-level action only as a recorded, supervisor-approved exception (maker-checker)

clauses.title: Minimum transaction amount

new.para: Annex III, 3(viii) (definition of Suspected Money Mule Transaction)
new.quote: “Suspected Money Mule Transaction” means a transaction of ₹ 1000 and above, flagged by the bank's transaction-monitoring systems (including AI / ML-based tools)

baseline.quote: The beneficiary bank or FI will put on hold an amount to the extent of the amount reported and update the same on CFCFRMS.

clauses.applies_to: Transactions the bank's own monitoring flags.
clauses.impact: The RBI DRAFT's floor only decides which bank-flagged transactions count as suspected. A CFCFRMS hold follows the reported amount, and Wapsi sets no minimum hold amount.
clauses.suggested_action: No rule change for CFCFRMS holds. Note the floor for any bank-initiated hold policy.

rules: A hold follows the tainted money on the trail; no minimum hold amount

clauses.title: Complaints about a hold

new.quote: Complaints shall be acknowledged on receipt and resolved within 30 days.

baseline.quote: submit such a grievance at the earliest and not beyond 07 calendar days from the day the aggrieved person complains.
update her decision on the Grievance Redressal Module within 15 calendar days of being notified.

clauses.applies_to: Complaints to the bank about bank-initiated holds.
clauses.impact: The RBI DRAFT gives the bank's own nodal officer 30 days to resolve a complaint about a bank-initiated hold. CFCFRMS grievances keep the SOP route and timelines through the IO and the District Grievance Officer.
clauses.suggested_action: No change for CFCFRMS holds. If bank-initiated holds are adopted, add a 30-day complaint-resolution clock for them.

clauses.title: Telling the account holder

new.quote: notify the account holder of the Temporary Debit Hold, stating reasons, the process for removal, and the concerned officer's contact details
the bank shall immediately notify the account holder, if communicating through digital mode, otherwise by EOD of the next day.

baseline.quote: Being initiated by a LEA, such sharing of information may not be considered as a tip-off

clauses.applies_to: Bank-initiated holds (a notice with reasons, the removal process and an officer's contact).
clauses.impact: The SOP allows the bank to tell the holder; the RBI DRAFT requires a notice with reasons, the removal process and an officer's contact, sent at once when digital. Wapsi drafts a customer notice (SMS, e-mail, letter) for each held account.
clauses.suggested_action: Check that the customer-notice template names the reason, the removal process and a contact officer, and that it goes out the same day by SMS or e-mail.

clauses.title: How long hold records are kept

new.quote: Related records shall be retained for a minimum of 5 years from the date of placing a temporary debit hold.
In case of an account closure, records shall be retained for a minimum period of 10 years from the closure.

clauses.baseline_note: The SOP sets no retention period for hold records of its own.
clauses.impact: If adopted, the audit trail of a bank-initiated hold must be kept for at least 5 years from the hold, or 10 years from account closure.
clauses.suggested_action: Set the retention of Wapsi's case audit log to cover the longer of the two periods before any bank-initiated hold goes live.

rules: Every approval and action is written to the case audit log

clauses.title: 2024 FRM Master Directions repealed

new.quote: the existing directions, instructions, and guidelines relating to Fraud Risk Management as applicable to Commercial Banks stand repealed
the 628 circulars listed in the Annex … are hereby repealed by the Reserve Bank with immediate effect.

new.para: Circulars Withdrawn by the Department of Supervision (DOS.CO.FMG.SEC.No.5/23.04.001/2024-25, 15.07.2024)
new.quote: Master Directions on Fraud Risk Management in Commercial Banks (including Regional Rural Banks) and All India Financial Institutions
The bank shall remain vigilant in monitoring transactions / unusual activities, specifically in the non-KYC compliant and money mule accounts

baseline.quote: Banks shall remain vigilant in monitoring transactions / unusual activities, specifically in the non-KYC compliant and money mule accounts etc.

clauses.impact: Para 67 repeals the earlier fraud-risk instructions for Commercial Banks by reference to circular DoS.CO.PPG.66; that circular repeals the circulars in its Annex, and RBI's withdrawn list for the Department of Supervision names the 2024 Master Directions. The money-mule monitoring duty carries over as para 24.
clauses.suggested_action: Done: Wapsi cites RBI-FRM-DIR-2026 (paras 12 and 24) and no longer cites the 2024 Master Directions. Keep checking new drafts for the retired id.
